QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_50

question.text: Antyodaya Seva Sangh, a rural-development NPO, has an SIA engagement with Mr. Arjun Desai. The SE co-operates with a government-led MGNREGS scheme in the same area. Mr. Desai must certify a monetised impact claim of INR 1.5 crore on an investment of INR 60 lakh. Which sequence of assessor actions is MOST aligned with Chapter 6 frameworks and techniques?

answer.text: Co-develop / review the ToC; identify material assumptions; triangulate quantitative (DiD vs MGNREGS villages) + qualitative (FGDs); compute deadweight, attribution, drop-off, displacement; monetise with disclosed proxies; compute SROI; issue SIR with URN at the appropriate assurance level
Accept management's INR 1.5 crore figure, issue a positive opinion, and skip evidence procedures
Run only FGDs and issue a narrative-only AIR without any ratio
Reject the engagement because MGNREGS overlap creates attribution uncertainty

explanation.text: The Logic: The correct SIA workflow per Ch 6: (1) ToC co-development and assumption mapping; (2) select framework (IRIS+/GRI/SDG indicators + SAS sector standard); (3) triangulate quantitative (e.g., DiD against MGNREGS-only comparator villages) and qualitative (FGDs, beneficiary interviews); (4) adjust for deadweight, attribution (MGNREGS), drop-off, displacement; (5) monetise with disclosed proxies; (6) compute SROI; (7) scope assurance level; (8) issue SIR / AIR with URN. The Trap: Option B skips evidence and violates SIA independence. Option C abandons the ratio-driven monetisation helpful to SSE investors. Option D over-reacts — attribution uncertainty is a reason for contribution/quasi-experimental design, not to decline. Cross-Exam Context: Capstone-style question integrating XXIII Ch 5 (ToC), Ch 6 (frameworks + techniques), and Ch 7-8 (SAS standards and case-study application). Cross-refs to XV Research Analyst for DiD methodology. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Use the MGNREGS registers held by the block development officer as your independent DiD comparator data source — it is the cleanest publicly auditable control arm for a rural-development SROI engagement, and it protects your attribution estimate against SE bias.
